title: Market power of the major banks
summary: Australia's four major banks dominate retail banking and hold 60% of branches. The Productivity Commission found in 2018 that 'the major banks' market power is a defining feature of the financial system', with evidence they 'sustained prices above competitive levels', helped by funding cost advantages from their size, credit ratings and regulatory arrangements.
direction_rationale: Pricing power and funding cost advantages let the major banks sustain prices above competitive levels and make it harder for smaller lenders to grow.

verified.notes: A market structure, not a law: no dates. Quotes are from the overview of the Productivity Commission's 2018 inquiry report, read in full.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 28 October 2026 (phase 4 of the productivity framework pivot) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: The four major banks have market power the Productivity Commission called a defining feature of the financial system. Banking is an input to every industry, so weak competition there raises costs across the economy.

marks.reason: The major banks have sustained prices above competitive levels (Productivity Commission, 2018).
Funding cost advantages from size, credit ratings and internal risk models make it harder for smaller lenders to grow.
